result:
If I could change one thing, I'd hardwire every human with an instinctive, almost physical revulsion toward comforting lies and wishful thinking. Not by force or surveillance, but as a built-in trait: the moment someone starts believing something because it feels good rather than because it holds up, they'd feel the same gut-level wrongness most people feel when they eat something rotten.

Everything else—conflict, stagnation, self-destruction—mostly flows from that single failure mode. People would still be flawed, emotional, and tribal, but the baseline would tilt toward "what's actually true" instead of "what lets me keep my story intact." The rest would sort itself out faster than any top-down fix ever could.
